Parley now builds and ships for Windows. This release attaches a Windows installer (`-setup.exe`) and an `.msi` alongside the macOS `.dmg`, both signed for the updater by the same key, so auto-update works on either platform.

The Windows build is an early one and it is honest about its limits: it records **your microphone only**. Capturing the other side of a call is a Core Audio process tap on macOS, and the Windows equivalent (WASAPI loopback) is not written yet — until it is, the parts of the app that depend on it, along with voice typing and the macOS permission walkthrough, stay hidden there rather than pretending to work. Everything else is the same app: transcription, diarization, the recording library, analysis, and the MCP server.

macOS is untouched by this release. The Windows work is behind a real platform layer instead of scattered checks — the window chrome, the settings panels, and the shortcut keys each ask one helper which OS they are on.
